course_description:
A studio-based course in which interdisciplinary teams of students develop a proposal for a significant software-based system. The course aims to consolidate and expand on students previous experience with designing information systems, user interfaces, and computer software and systems. Subjects such as requirements elicitation, business cases, design specifications, and identifying and dealing with professional and ethical issues associated with software projects and products are covered during the course.

DECO7380 is one of two level 3 studio project courses for UQ's Master of Information Technology and Master of Interaction Design programs, with the other being DECO7381. In these two courses, students work in teams on project areas which are derived by the teams themselves from course resources and elsewhere. DECO7380 incorporates the problem finding, ideation, design and user requirements gathering leading to a proposed solution. DECO7381 starts from the design brief/proposal and allows other teams of students to further design, build, and evaluate them.

As a studio course, DECO7380 involves creative, divergent, reflective and critical design activities that explore the nature of a problem or challenge space and identify possible solutions/opportunities for digital technologies. These activities lead to a proposal for a design that a different team of students in DECO7381 could prototype.

AI tools may be used to support learning and task completion in this course, and the course provides guidance on appropriate use. Students are expected to apply judgement when using these tools, to check outputs carefully, and to ensure that all submitted work reflects their own understanding. Students are responsible for ensuring that any use of AI complies with academic integrity requirements and is appropriately acknowledged.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

The assessment has been simplified to remove the journal and associated hurdle. Weekly in-person check-in activities and the research portfolio interview are introduced to assist with tracking progress and meeting secure assessment policy requirements.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with experience in the software design lifecycle, with an emphasis on problem finding and eliciting requirements from a broad problem domain or challenge area, leading to the production of a well-specified and justified system design supported by appropriate low/medium-fidelity prototypes and design documentation.ﾠ Student teams apply contemporary project management tools and techniques in the context of a larger-scale design process.ﾠ As a capstone studio course, students are given the opportunity to apply and further develop their technical and design skills acquired in other courses and elsewhere.

learning_outcomes.description: Synthesise a significant digital solution to an identified problem in the world, overcoming challenges associated with implementing new designs and technologies leading to a clearly documented design proposal.

Apply and consolidate previous experience and skills in human-centred design and software development to develop representations of the design concept at different levels of fidelity in order to better communicate with stakeholders and to clarify and inform project requirements.

Apply sound project management methods and techniques to improve the outcomes of software design projects, where the relative merits of the methods are critiqued and adapted for the project context, making use of relevant tools for strategic planning and scheduling where appropriate.
Communicate effectively with stakeholders to gather requirements and understand the problem context, and to manage expectations over the course of a project.

Demonstrate an ability to work successfully in a multi-disciplinary team and reflectively apply methods and techniques for effective collaborative teamwork, including digital tools and platforms, resolving conflicts where they arise.
Examine and question ethical and professional issues associated with technology projects or products and apply ethical thinking to your own work.

Critically reflect on the relationship between practical and theoretical aspects of design through detailed examination of project work in relation to published literature [THIS LEARNING OBJECTIVE CONTRIBUTES TO AQF9 RESEARCH FOR MASTERS PROGRAMS]

assessment_details.task_description: The primary focus of this Studio course is a team-based project in which students identify a problem, investigate the problem context, and develop a documented design that can be used by another team to implement a working prototype in DECO3801/7381. Project assessment consists of a sequence of design checkpoints throughout the semester, including Problem Identification , Interim Project Critique , and the Final Exhibit and Documentation . Each checkpoint includes an in-class presentation and the submission of project documentation, with the documentation progressively developed into the project's final design/requirements document. Feedback provided during the early checkpoints is formative and intended to support students in refining their work. The final project grade is determined holistically, considering the quality of the final outcome together with the design process demonstrated throughout the semester. Detailed assessment requirements and submission instructions are provided in the assessment briefs on Blackboard. Use of Generative AI This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI will provide only limited support and guidance. Failure to acknowledge AI/MT use or demonstrate authorship and understanding of the submission may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct and may result in penalties of up to the total marks available for the assessment. Detailed guidance is provided in the assessment brief and on Blackboard. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.task_description: The Research Portfolio is the major individual assessment for Studio 3 and provides the primary evidence of your learning, individual contribution, and professional development throughout the semester. This research portfolio also contributes to the research requirements for masters programs where students are not undertaking an individual thesis research project. Your research portfolio should present a curated selection of work that demonstrates your contribution to the team project, your design process, and your learning. It should include critical reflection on your decisions, challenges and outcomes, rather than simply showcasing completed work. Regardless of the focus, the portfolio must also connect and reflect on relevant research literature with the student's personal experience in their studio project. The Research Portfolio will be assessed on the quality and coherence of the submission, evidence of your individual contribution, the depth of reflection and research, and the authenticity of the work presented. Throughout the semester, you will complete individual Exit Slips to support reflection on your progress and contribution. Exit Slips provide formative feedback and contribute to the evidence used to assess your research portfolio and individual engagement. Detailed requirements, submission instructions, and expectations for the Research Portfolio and Exit Slips are provided in the assessment brief on Blackboard.
